issues: The whole shot was a grey placeholder dashboard full of grey bars: no readable word, no sense of what the product is
The Deploy button had 18px text and floated on a card corner; even at 1.4x the subject stayed small and the frame had no centre of gravity
The click only swapped the button label; after the pull-back the frame looked like the opening, so cause and effect never landed
The cursor was small with a short path, so the wrist-flick overshoot barely read
changes: Sand look (warm beige, terracotta): the subject is now a purpose-built stay booking card, Quinta do Vale, spanning 78% of the frame, with a procedurally drawn hillside sunset (five ridges with aerial perspective, cypresses, a villa, drifting birds)

New typography: 92px title, 132px price, 36px trip details and a wide-tracked terracotta kicker; the 560x112 primary button with 42px text is the only dark block in a warm light frame, so its hover brightening reads

The cursor is 76px and enters on a Bezier from off-frame bottom-left, flicks past the button along its tangent at f36 and swings back in 6f, with speed tilt and directional blur; it moves aside during the pull-back to reveal the result

Rhythm: 14f expo-out punch-in 1 to 1.42, a 24f hold that plays out the consequence (Holding your dates spinner, then Reserved with the face turning terracotta and the price note changing), then a 20f symmetric pull-back
As the camera settles, an ink confirmation bar springs up (Sep 14 - 17 is yours.), so the last frame is a complete poster of the outcome; the hold keeps a slow 1.5% push
The ripple is a terracotta ring (24f out-cubic growth decoupled from a 28f linear fade) plus one press glow clipped to the button radius
